items.text: V_J(K')=\{\varepsilon\in\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(P_I,K') : \varepsilon|_J=0\}
V_J(K')\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(P_I/J,\,K')\qquad\text{functorially in }K'
Definitions
$V_J$: closed algebraic subspace of $E^I$. A functor isomorphic to some $V_J$: affine algebraic space over $K$.
Affine algebraic spaces are representable (by $P_I/J$). Conversely, let $A$ be a $K$-algebra.
$A\simeq P_I/J$ iff there is a surjective $\varphi\colon P_I\to A$ with $\ker\varphi=J$.
\varphi\leftrightarrow (a_i)_{i\in I},\ a_i=\varphi(T_i);\qquad \varphi \text{ surjective}\iff (a_i)\text{ generates }A
Affine algebraic spaces over $K$ = representable functors. An embedding of $V_A$ into $E^I$ as a closed subspace = a family of generators of $A$ indexed by $I$.
Intrinsic study $\leftrightarrow$ arbitrary $K$-algebras; extrinsic study $\leftrightarrow$ an algebra with a set of generators.
Morphisms $V_J\to V_{J'}$
$J\subset P_I$, $J'\subset P_{I'}$. A morphism = natural transformation: for $K'\to K''$ the squares
\begin{CD} V_J(K') @>>> V_{J'}(K')\\ @VVV @VVV\\ V_J(K'') @>>> V_{J'}(K'') \end{CD}
commute.
Polynomial maps $E^I\to E^{I'}$: $E^{I'}=(E^1)^{I'}$, given by $(f_{i'})_{i'\in I'}$, $f_{i'}\in P_I$.
Claim: every morphism $V_J\to V_{J'}$ is induced by a polynomial map $E^I\to E^{I'}$ carrying $V_J$ into $V_{J'}$.
V_J=h_A,\ A=P_I/J;\qquad V_{J'}=h_{A'},\ A'=P_{I'}/J'
\operatorname{Hom}(h_A,h_{A'})\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(A',A)
$\varphi\colon A'\to A$ $\leftrightarrow$ $\psi\colon P_{I'}\to A$ vanishing on $J'$ $\leftrightarrow$ a family $(a_{i'})\in A^{I'}$.
Lift $a_{i'}$ to $F_{i'}\in P_I$ ($A=P_I/J$): $P_{I'}\to P_I$, $T_{i'}\mapsto F_{i'}$, maps $J'$ into $J$ and passes to the quotient $A'\to A$.
(F_{i'})_{i'\in I'}\colon E^I\to E^{I'},\qquad F_{i'}\in P_I,\quad F(V_J)\subset V_{J'}
Embeddings of $V_A$ in $E^I$
$E^I=V_{P_I}$; a morphism $V_A\to E^I$ $\leftrightarrow$ $P_I\to A$, i.e. elements $(a_i)\in A^I$.
$V_A\to E^I$ is a monomorphism iff $P_I\to A$ is an epimorphism of rings; it suffices that it be surjective, but this is not necessary.
Example: an epimorphism that is not surjective
K[T]\hookrightarrow K[T,T^{-1}],\quad T\mapsto T\qquad (K\neq 0)
\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(K[T,T^{-1}],K')\ \simeq\ K'^{\times}\ \subset\ K'\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(K[T],K')
$T^{-1}$ is not in the image of $K[T]$: not surjective, but $V_A\to E^1$ is a monomorphism, not an isomorphism onto a closed subspace (it is an open embedding).
